title: Text and date functions
explanation: Meet a new table: players, the people who play the games. A function is a mini tool that changes a value. Text functions: UPPER() makes text capital letters, LOWER() makes it small letters, and LENGTH() counts the characters. You can also glue text together with || (two straight lines). Dates are stored as text like '2021-03-14' (year-month-day). To pull out a piece of a date, use strftime(): strftime('%Y', signup_date) gives the year, and strftime('%m', signup_date) gives the month. Heads-up: other databases write this differently, like YEAR(signup_date), but the idea is the same.

lines.explain: Turn each username into small letters, and nickname that column small_name.
Pull the month out of the sign-up date, and nickname it signup_month.

tasks.prompt: Show every username in capital letters. Name the column loud_name.
tasks.answer: SELECT UPPER(username) AS loud_name FROM players;
hints: Which function turns text into capital letters?

solution_lines.explain: Turn each username into capitals, nicknamed loud_name.

tasks.prompt: Show each username and how many characters it has. Name the new column name_length.
tasks.answer: SELECT username, LENGTH(username) AS name_length FROM players;

solution_lines.explain: Show the username, plus how many characters it has, nicknamed name_length.

tasks.prompt: Show each username and the year they signed up. Name the new column signup_year.
tasks.answer: SELECT username, strftime('%Y', signup_date) AS signup_year FROM players;
hints: Use strftime() with the code for year.

solution_lines.line: SELECT username, strftime('%Y', signup_date) AS signup_year
solution_lines.explain: Show the username, plus the year pulled out of the sign-up date.

tasks.prompt: Show the username and hours played of players who signed up in 2021, most hours first.
tasks.answer: SELECT username, hours_played FROM players WHERE strftime('%Y', signup_date) = '2021' ORDER BY hours_played DESC;
hints: Use strftime() in your WHERE line. The year comes out as text, so put 2021 in single quotes.
WHERE strftime('%Y', signup_date) = '2021' ORDER BY hours_played DESC

solution_lines.explain: Show me the username and hours played columns.
Keep players whose sign-up year is 2021. It's in quotes because strftime gives back text.
Sort by hours played, most first.

tasks.prompt: Make one column called tag that looks like ShadowFox (USA), but only for usernames longer than 8 characters.
tasks.answer: SELECT username || ' (' || country || ')' AS tag FROM players WHERE LENGTH(username) > 8;
hints: Glue the pieces together with ||: the username, then ' (', then the country, then ')'. Then filter with LENGTH().
SELECT username || ' (' || country || ')' AS tag ... WHERE LENGTH(username) > 8

solution_lines.explain: Glue together the username, a space and bracket, the country, and a closing bracket. Nickname it tag.
Keep only usernames with more than 8 characters.

recap: You just learned text functions (UPPER, LOWER, LENGTH), how to glue text with ||, and how to pull the year or month out of a date with strftime().
